newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end up, gasoline holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end up, gasoline holds support.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices seesawed into a positive end Thursday after spot gasoline held technical support amid views of rising gasoline demand.

"I think the price action reflects the fact that gasoline inventories are still below a year ago and the demand is picking up," said John Bradberry, vice president at Transmontaigne Products Services Inc, a petroleum distributor in Fayettville, Arkansas.
May gasoline ended up 0.32 cent at 60.70 cents a gallon.
Spot gasoline rebounded off of its key 60.00 cent support area twice, oscillating between positive and negative territory throughout the session.
May crude ended seven cents higher a barrel at $19.42 after falling as low as $19.10. May heating oil ended 0.52 cent up at 54.00 cents a gallon, rebounding from its session low of 53.20.
Dealers noted unseasonably cold weather in several U.S. regions has created a slow start to spring when there is a seasonal uptick in gasoline demand leading up to the summer driving season.
But, the demand picture is changing, dealers said.

"Locally gasoline demand has really begun to pick up, and I assume that will start to be true in other places as well," said Bradberry, noting Midwest gasoline retailers are already lining up stocks for the summer.
Earlier this month, the U.S. Department of Energy said it expected gasoline demand to grow by 1.8 percent this summer, leading traders to buy gasoline on price dips.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said gasoline stocks as of April 11 were 1.97 million barrels below a year ago.
Meanwhile, heating oil prices have remained firm all week as cold tempertures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States were seen persisting into next week.
In fact, Sun Co said increased demand due to the lower temperatures has drained its heating oil inventories, and that it was unlikely to resume supplying to distributors until late next week.
The National Weather Service forecasted below normal temperatures in the Northeast in its six-to-10 day forecast starting April 21.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
